clue.text: Does fare include the hour out in coaches?

indicators.note: the hour is put out of the coaches, so its abbreviation is removed from that word

parts.note: coaches hired for a trip are charters
HR is the standard abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether the coach ticket price covers an hour's outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' is a link word here; taking HR out of CHARTERS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides food, so one who caters supplies fare in the sense of meals.

clue.text: Standard raised by Petty Officer, held by Captain

indicators.note: the reversed pair is held inside the captain

parts.note: Captain James Cook, the explorer

indicators.note: in a down clue raised reads the letters from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Naval standards are kept up by a petty officer under a captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works because this is a down clue, so the letters read upwards make OPYB. 'Standard' is an adjective here: exemplary.
explanation.definitionFit: Copybook as an adjective means exemplary, matching a standard model to be copied.

clue.text: Illustrator capturing ecstasy in emphatic scoreline

indicators.note: the scoreline captures the drug, holding it inside

parts.note: ten-nil is a resounding football score
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a drug-fuelled thrashing on the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside TEN-NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: John Tenniel was the Victorian artist who drew the original pictures for Alice in Wonderland.

clue.text: Pithy stuff put right around chest muscle when lifting

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting reads the whole assembly from bottom to top
the repair word goes around the chest muscle

parts.note: to repair is to put right
pec, short for pectoral, is a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A gym-goer works out the chest by lifting weights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when lifting' turns the whole REPAPECIR upwards, as this is a down clue; 'Pithy' is literal, not meaning concise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice paper is made from the pith of a tree, so it is literally pithy stuff.

clue.text: It's lucky there's room for sentiment in publicity work

indicators.note: an advert that has room for something holds it inside, so this signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: AD, short for advertisement, is publicity
goo is sloppy sentimentality
a job is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Advertising work leaves space for sentimental touches, which is fortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's room for' sits between the pieces as the container signal; 'sentiment' is mushy feeling, slang goo.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation said when something turns out fortunately, idiomatic for a happy escape.

clue.text: Daring beetle going under bark

definitions.meaning: bold and innovative, doing something never done before
a beetle burrowing beneath bark is literally breaking into the ground of the tree

explanation.surface: A bold insect bores beneath a tree's bark.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a cryptic picture of a boring beetle literally breaking new ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneering work that breaks new ground is daring and original.

clue.text: Start shooting here

definitions.meaning: filming takes place on the film set

explanation.surface: A director calls action at the location.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginning is an onset; filming happens on set, the place where shooting is done.

clue.text: Drive by thieves to have ordinary bloke pinch your identity

indicators.note: the bloke pinches the letters, gripping them inside

parts.note: Joe, as in Joe Bloggs or Joe Public, is the ordinary man
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A thief steals someone's identity before taking a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinch' looks like theft but means grip tight; 'Drive by thieves' is a drive taken by car thieves, not a drive-by shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyride is a reckless drive in a stolen car, so a drive taken by thieves.

clue.text: Versifying Rupert Bear for the radio

indicators.note: for the radio means as heard spoken on air

parts.note: to bear is to tolerate, to brook

explanation.surface: A cartoon bear named Rupert performs poetry on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a British children's comic character, but here Rupert is the war poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was the First World War poet, so he is a Rupert who wrote verse.

clue.text: Upstart paparazzo pursuing one with punishing schedule?

indicators.note: the paparazzo follows the punisher, so comes after

parts.note: one who whips is a whipper
a paparazzo is a press photographer, a snapper

explanation.surface: A celebrity photographer hounds someone with a gruelling timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is a presumptuous young person, a cheeky upstart.

clue.text: He paid through the nose for his pork pies

definitions.text: He paid through the nose for his pork pies

parts.words: He paid through the nose for his pork pies
parts.note: pork pies is rhyming slang for lies, and this puppet's nose grew longer each time he told one, so he paid with his nose

explanation.surface: Someone was overcharged for some savoury pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pies' is Cockney rhyming slang for lies; a pork pie is a British cold meat pastry. 'Paid through the nose' (paid too much) is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden puppet in Collodi's story whose nose grows with every lie fits the literal reading.

clue.text: Authority makes no comment

parts.note: to make a comment is to say something, so read as says
no, or nothing, is the letter O, which looks like zero

explanation.surface: A person in power declines to comment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'says nothing': SAYS plus O for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the say-so means having the power to decide, so it is a synonym for authority.

clue.text: Grave wish to keep time in dance music

indicators.note: the grave wish with its time sits in the dance word, inside it

parts.note: bop is to dance

indicators.note: the grave wish keeps time, holding it within its letters

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the wish on a gravestone

explanation.surface: A tombstone's wish keeps the beat in a dance track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance' looks like part of the definition 'dance music', but it supplies the bop that holds everything; 'to keep' and 'in' are the two container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Britpop was a 1990s genre of British guitar pop music, so it is a kind of music.

clue.text: Zealous critics do make lousy choice?

parts.note: lousy literally means infested with lice, whose eggs are nits
a pick is a choice

explanation.surface: Keen reviewers make a poor selection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lousy choice' read literally is a choice of nits, a nit pick; fussy critics do just that.
explanation.definitionFit: Overzealous critics fuss over trivial faults, which is what nit-picking means.

clue.text: Right to separate duck, dock and deck

indicators.note: right comes between the duck and the dock, separating them

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O
to dock is to cut short, to lop

explanation.surface: The right way to distinguish a duck, a dock and a deck.
explanation.walkthrough: R splits O and LOP. A duck is a batter's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, so the answer names a deck.

clue.text: English doctor departs after a career is taken up

indicators.note: departs comes after career, so its letter follows

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
to career is to rush or race
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An English doctor leaves after their professional path is taken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb meaning to rush, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or cause is to take it up readily, so these past forms match.

clue.text: A-road comes across as quiet way to travel on the surface

definitions.text: way to travel on the surface

indicators.note: A LANE comes across the other letters, spanning them

parts.note: taken as A and road, a lane
a road is a lane
qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A main road appears to be a calm route across the land.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-road is a major British main road, here split as A plus a road; 'comes across' means spans the Latin as and quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To aquaplane is to skim on the surface of water, as a vehicle on a wet road does.

clue.text: Attempt to arrest one applying squeeze, avoiding extreme violence

indicators.note: the attempt arrests the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: losing its final letter, the extreme end

parts.note: one who squeezes in an embrace is a hugger

explanation.surface: Trying to arrest an enforcer while avoiding excessive force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extreme violence' looks like one phrase, but 'avoiding extreme' cuts the last letter, giving HUGGE; 'to arrest' means hold inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuggery is brutal violent behaviour, typical of thugs.

clue.text: Flower in leaf transformed S knitting pattern

indicators.note: the flower sits in the rearranged leaf
the letters of leaf are transformed into a new order

parts.note: an iris is a flower

explanation.surface: A flower inside a leaf becomes a knitting design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges LEAF into FALE; the stray S is the possessive 's of the printed clue, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is a style of multicoloured knitting named after a Shetland island.

clue.text: Summons heard as a rule

indicators.note: heard tells us the words are spoken and their sound counts

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: A court summons is read out as a general rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a charge, so it summons them.

clue.text: Vague approval from assortment of upper-class Henrys

indicators.note: an assortment mixes the letters together in a new order

parts.note: U is the standard label for upper-class; applied to two of the Henrys it gives two of them
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance; plural Henrys gives several

explanation.surface: Some posh men named Henry give a lukewarm nod.
explanation.walkthrough: The henry is the SI unit of inductance, symbol H; U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The noncommittal grunt people make to show half-hearted agreement is vague approval.

clue.text: Beheaded freak blocking Queen's succession

indicators.note: the freak is blocking the Queen's letters, stuck between them

parts.note: HM, Her Majesty's, is the Queen's

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a weirdo is a freak

explanation.surface: A headless oddball stands in the way of the royal line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' leaves EIRDO; the Queen's is HM, Her Majesty's, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirdom is the state of being heir, hence succession to an inheritance.

clue.text: Lift record breaking poetry reading from this

indicators.note: in a down clue lift raises the letters to read bottom to top
the record breaks into the poetry, splitting it

parts.note: odes are poems, poetry
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A lift sets a record during a poetry recital.
explanation.walkthrough: EP goes into ODES to give ODEEPS, and 'Lift' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedometer is the dial you take a speed reading from, so it is what 'this' refers to.

clue.text: Efficient flesh remover in Pennsylvania State hospital

indicators.note: the state and hospital go in Pennsylvania's abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
Iran is a nation state

explanation.surface: A ruthless surgeon works in a state hospital in Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like part of a US hospital name, but it is the country IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American fish strips flesh from its prey with sharp teeth, a vivid description.

clue.text: Wilderness below Tyneside upset Greens

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed greens go below the Tyneside letters

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down

parts.note: veg, short for vegetables, are greens

explanation.surface: Environmentalists are upset in a wild area below Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England. VEG turned up gives GEV.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is a desert in southern Israel, a wilderness.

clue.text: Writer turning left into parking and crashing

indicators.note: turning one thing into another replaces it, so left becomes parking

parts.note: Rudyard Kipling is the writer
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: An author swerves left into a car park and has an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' is slang for sleeping, not a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash is slang for falling asleep, and kipping is British slang for sleeping too.

clue.text: They in general keep watching

indicators.note: the words keep the answer, holding it within their letters

explanation.surface: People generally stay on watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To be eyeing something is to be looking at it, so it means watching.

clue.text: Beg for passage through neighbouring land

definitions.meaning: to ask passers-by for money in the street
a narrow strip of a territory running out between neighbouring regions

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for the right of way across a neighbour's property.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for street begging and a noun for a thin strip of territory jutting out.

clue.text: One fancies most things new in novel or movie

indicators.note: novel means new or unusual, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A reader who likes almost everything, new in books and films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal for N, OR and MOVIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that eats almost anything 'fancies' most foods, a playful take on an all-eater.

clue.text: Not having long, teacher morally obliged to cancel exam every semester

indicators.note: the teacher is not having the long, so that word is removed

parts.note: to long for is to ache

indicators.note: the morally obliged person cancels the exam, removing it

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A teacher with little time feels bound to call off a test each term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is a verb meaning yearn. TEACHER less ACHE leaves TER; MORALLY less ORAL leaves MLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Termly means once each school term, and a semester is a term.
